# Gramlot 0.3.5 — Quantize external slider values through the binding

Horizontal and vertical sliders now correct finite external Data values according to their native min/max/step constraints. With step=1, a splitter value of 176.73 becomes 177 in the shared Data, keeping the slider, panel and labels aligned. Initial values and reactive range changes follow the same rule.

Equal values are not rewritten; synchronous correction is guarded against reentrancy. Literal/read-only bindings and other input controls retain their contracts. No splitter-specific step or application synchronization controller is introduced. Shared controls require compatible ranges.

Verified with the core regression suite, Python metadata and Chromium/WebKit browser tests covering exact write counts, fractional steps, reactive limits, linked sliders and real splitter dragging. The l05 gallery regression covers all seven size bindings.
